choices.why: A true light grey three-seater, 234 cm wide, with clean tailored lines that fill the long left wall without crowding it.
A large 200x300 plain beige flatweave that defines the seating area from sofa to TV and stays light and easy to clean when friends come over.
Light ash with slim tapered legs, exactly the light wood the user asked for, and airy enough to keep the room bright.
A low white console with open shelves that blends into the white walls and keeps the room looking clean, modern and bright.
The black arc lamp echoes the black frame of the balcony door and reaches over the sofa with warm, sociable light.
A pair of terracotta cushions gives the pop of color the user wants against the light grey sofa, and their neutral tassels tie in with the rug.
A tall, leafy areca palm by the balcony door adds height and fresh green, and it thrives in this much light.
A pair of white light-filtering panels softens the black-framed sliding door while keeping the living room bright.

answer.why: A light palette of grey, beige, white and light ash keeps the room bright and modern, with black accents that repeat the window frame. The terracotta cushions and the green palm add warmth and color for having friends over.
